312d267d182c1ce1: PAS Youth’s annual muktamar opened two weeks ago with a multicultural drum performance – a rare sight at the Islamic party’s annual assembly. The performance combined traditional drums from Malay, Chinese, Indian and Thai cultures.

This was very different from previous assemblies, particularly given PAS’s identity as a Malay-Muslim party. Obviously, Malaysians generally viewed it as another attempt at boosting PAS’s image among non-Muslim communities as the next general election approaches.

The Islamic party has often turned to symbolic gestures such as this. Here, they invited everyone to feel the rhythm of shared unity. Honestly, it was a beautiful image with hands of different colours striking the same skin of a drum, bodies swaying in sync, a moment of transcendent harmony.

On the surface, it seemed like the perfect antidote to a worsening division in the country, brought about mainly by the pronouncements of its top leaders on how non-Muslims must play a secondary role in the governance of Malaysia.
But here’s the uncomfortable truth we rarely admit. The drumbeat is not a bridge but often a band-aid. It offers a feeling of unity that ends the moment the performance stops.

The performance may have made the youth wing feel it had done something significant about racism when, in reality, the togetherness lasted only for an hour. The next day, everyone returned to the same segregated schools and unequal opportunities, with politicians once again harping on race and religion. Racial unity needs structural intervention, not a sonic spectacle.
If PAS is serious about racial unity – seemingly the party’s lowest priority – it must stop treating it as a performance and start treating it as a structural commitment.

Unity is not something you feel in your chest during a drum performance, but something you build in your community through policy, accountability and willingness to sit in discomfort, not dance in rhythm.
The question centres on whether the party’s use of multi-ethnic cultural elements in its opening ceremonies is merely cosmetic, given deeper concerns about minority rights in its policy platform.

The underlying sentiment reflected in social media by critics reveals a deep-seated distrust among minority communities for the Islamic party, rooted in historical and ongoing political wounds. Most non-Malays viewed this as scratching the surface while the wounds are already deep – a broader crisis of trust in Malaysian politics.
This distrust is not new, as it is rooted in decades of ethnically charged politics made worse by PAS leader Abdul Hadi Awang’s constant push for Malay-Muslim supremacy.

To make it worse, PAS’s so-called multiracial political friends like Barisan Nasional and Wawasan have remained silent over the near-seditious pronouncements of Hadi. Even Rafizi Ramli’s Bersama, which has openly promised to push for more equality, has chosen to remain silent as it obviously does not want to lose any Malay support before even taking off politically.
Say it in the manifesto
The real challenge for PAS or any other political party is to move beyond cosmetic gestures and come out openly with substantive policy assurances that protect the rights of all citizens.
Here, manifestos play an important role. They serve as crucial documents published by parties before general elections, setting out the policies they would deliver if elected.

They convey a party’s wider narrative and the background to its policy choices. While governments have no statutory obligation to fulfil manifesto commitments – as we have seen in all general elections – there are strong political reasons to adhere to them, as they bring credibility and demonstrate understanding of societal challenges.
So, can PAS declare in its manifesto that its ultimate aim is to make Malaysia an Islamic state when it comes to power or leads a ruling coalition at the federal level?

Will it openly declare that it will ban all forms of gambling? With its delegates calling for a PAS minister to oversee Kuala Lumpur if it comes to power, will the party also declare that it will give the capital’s landscape a more Islamic outlook? Or like what its supreme leader Hadi has been constantly preaching, will non-Malay ministers be barred from heading key policymaking portfolios? And how will it tackle the problem of unlicensed places of worship if and when it comes to power?

If the party wins power after putting these down in writing in its manifesto, it can be viewed as what the majority of Malaysians want. No individual or party should protest if this happens, as the voters would be choosing with their eyes open. As they say, the people deserve the government they choose.

In modern democracies, the extent to which pre-election policy promises translate into actual policymaking is a key factor in political legitimisation. We are seeing how Pakatan Harapan is struggling after failing in this aspect.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
e94124b4f10bc2a4: PETALING JAYA: Few fish have been handed a worse public image than the piranha. Mention the name and many people picture a river boiling with razor-toothed fish stripping flesh from bone in seconds.
So when a fish suspected to be a piranha was caught at Klau Dam in Raub, Pahang on Aug 26, it was hardly surprising that social media lit up.
The fisheries department has since said there is no evidence of an established or breeding piranha population in the dam, and no further suspected fish had been caught as of Sept 15.
The fish itself was no longer available for examination, but photographs and video were judged to have features consistent with the genus Pygocentrus, one of the best-known piranha groups.
So, how much of their fearsome reputation is deserved? Here are seven fascinating facts about this supposedly fearsome fish.
1. Piranhas are not native to Malaysia

Piranhas are freshwater fish native to South America, especially river systems connected to the Amazon basin. That means any piranha found in Malaysian waters would be an introduced species rather than part of the natural ecosystem.

This is why the fisheries department has warned against releasing alien fish into rivers, lakes and reservoirs. Even an exotic pet that seems harmless in an aquarium can create ecological problems if it survives and reproduces in the wild.
For now, there is no evidence that this has happened at Klau Dam.
2. Yes, they eat flesh - but that is only part of the menu
Piranhas do have sharp teeth and some species certainly eat flesh. But their diet is much broader than pop culture would have you believe.

Red-bellied piranhas, for example, may feed on small fish, bits of flesh, insects, aquatic invertebrates and even plant material such as fruit. A significant part of their diet can also come from nipping pieces from the fins of larger fish.
So while “flesh-eating fish” is not exactly false, it leaves out a lot of context.
3. They are far less likely to devour people than films suggest

Scientific reviews have found very little evidence for the classic image of piranhas swarming and consuming healthy humans. Most documented injuries involve a single bite, often to bathers or swimmers, and are thought to be linked to territorial behaviour or protection of nests and young.
A recent review of more than 700 reported piranha bites in Brazil found that over 80% were mild, with many involving isolated “punch-out” wounds rather than frenzied attacks.
That does not make piranhas harmless, but it does put the threat in perspective.
4. Some ‘man-eating’ cases involved people who were already dead
This is one of the stranger facts behind the legend.

A scientific review of documented incidents found that several cases in which piranhas were said to have “eaten” humans involved people who had already died from causes such as drowning or heart failure before the fish began scavenging.
That is very different from a healthy swimmer being overwhelmed by a school of hungry fish.
5. Their teeth really are impressive
Piranhas do have a formidable bite: their triangular, interlocking teeth are designed for slicing and shearing, which helps explain why even a single bite can cause a distinctive chunk-like wound.
The teeth are one reason their reputation has endured so successfully, but the anatomy does not mean they are constantly hunting large animals - or people.
6. Hollywood has done wonders for their bad reputation

Piranhas have enjoyed a surprisingly long career as horror villains. Best-known film series include "Piranha" (1978), "Piranha II: The Spawning" (1982), "Piranha 3D" (2010) and, mind-bogglingly, "Piranha 3DD" (2012).
The original arrived in the wave of creature features that followed "Jaws", replacing the shark with something smaller but, on screen at least, considerably more numerous.
And there is a nice piece of film trivia tucked into the franchise: "Piranha II" was an early directing credit for James Cameron, years before "Titanic" and "Avatar".
No wonder generations of moviegoers grew up regarding any vaguely toothy freshwater fish with suspicion.
7. The real issue in Malaysia may be ecological, not cinematic
The Klau Dam report is intriguing, but so far it points to one suspected fish, not an invasion.
The fisheries department says continued monitoring has not found further evidence of piranhas or related safety incidents, and has even released a visual comparing it to the more innocuous ikan pacu.

So, again, this makes the bigger concern less about swimmers being eaten and more about what happens when exotic species are released into local waterways. Introduced fish can compete with native species, prey on them, alter food webs and potentially affect biodiversity if they become established.

For anyone who catches an unfamiliar exotic fish, the advice from the department is simple: do not release it back into the water. Keep the specimen if possible, and contact the nearest fisheries office so it can be properly examined.
3b2d3b701cd20836: PETALING JAYA: Tumpuan PAS dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) terhadap 126 kerusi Parlimen menunjukkan gabungan itu sedang membuat persiapan sendiri menghadapi PRU16, langkah yang berpotensi menjejaskan rundingan kerjasama dengan Umno, kata penganalisis.

Mazlan Ali dari Universiti Teknologi Malaysia berkata kenyataan Ketua Penerangan PN Annuar Musa mengenai persiapan itu menimbulkan persoalan sama ada kerjasama antara Umno dan PAS benar-benar dapat direalisasikan pada pilihan raya umum akan datang.
“Kalau dengar kenyataan Annuar, ia membayangkan kerjasama PAS dan Umno mungkin tidak berlaku.
“Keadaan menjadi lebih sukar apabila Umno menyatakan mereka mahu kerjasama strategik dengan PAS sahaja, bukan dengan parti dalam PN,” katanya kepada FMT.

Mazlan berkata pendekatan itu juga selari dengan aspirasi PAS sebelum ini untuk mempertahankan semua kerusi Parlimen dimenanginya pada PRU15 serta memperkukuh kedudukannya sebagai parti utama dalam pentadbiran negara.
Pada PRU15, PN memenangi 74 kerusi Parlimen, dengan PAS menguasai 43 daripadanya.

Minggu lalu, Annuar yang juga Ahli Jawatankuasa PAS Pusat berkata jentera pilihan raya PAS dan PN memberi tumpuan kepada persiapan di 126 kerusi Parlimen yang dikenal pasti mempunyai potensi tinggi, tidak termasuk kawasan di Sarawak.
Beliau bagaimanapun menjelaskan PAS tidak semestinya bertanding di semua 126 kerusi itu kerana sebahagiannya mungkin ditandingi parti sekutu.
Sementara itu, Tawfik Yaakub dari Universiti Malaya berpandangan sasaran untuk memenangi keseluruhan 126 kerusi itu sukar dicapai sekiranya PN berdepan pertandingan tiga penjuru atau lebih.
Menurutnya, persiapan berasingan seperti itu juga berisiko menjejaskan persefahaman politik yang sedang dibina bersama Umno menerusi beberapa pilihan raya negeri.

Beliau berkata kerjasama politik antara Barisan Nasional (BN) dan PN, sama ada menerusi persefahaman atau bentuk kerjasama lain, boleh menjadi faktor penting dalam usaha mana-mana blok mencapai majoriti mudah 112 kerusi di Dewan Rakyat.
“Untuk membentuk kerajaan dominan oleh sebuah gabungan politik semata-mata dalam dinamik politik Malaysia hari ini hanyalah mimpi dan angan-angan,” katanya.
Umno sebelum ini memberi isyarat bahawa rundingan politik menjelang PRU16 lebih cenderung dilakukan secara langsung dengan PAS berbanding PN secara keseluruhan.
fb9ba70515b9099a: MUNICH: Harry Kane scored twice in Bayern Munich's 7-0 demolition of Union Berlin on Friday , becoming the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals.
Kane scored his 100th and 101st goals in just 98 domestic games, obliterating the previous record set by Cologne's Dieter Mueller in 1977 by 31 games.
It's the latest record that the England captain has torn up during his time in Munich, having already become the fastest Bayern player to reach 75, 100 and 150 goals in all competitions.
Kane's double means he now has scored 156 goals in 156 games for Bayern in domestic and international games combined - an unparalleled statistic.
"I'm very proud to reach 101 Bundesliga goals," Kane told Sky Germany.
"In the short time I've been here, I've loved every second of it. When I'm playing with these players - Michael (Olise), Luis (Diaz) and Jamal (Musiala), I'm going to get chances.
"To have more goals than games is obviously a great stat to have," he added.

When asked about his Bayern contract, which expires at the end of the season, and whether he'll still be at the club when the Champions League final returns to Munich in 2028, Kane said: "I'm extremely happy here.
"The talks are ongoing and they'll be ongoing for the near future. You can see the way I'm playing and the way I connect with the fans.
"Munich in 2028? Maybe. It'll be a special one."
Despite Kane's record-breaking exploits, Michael Olise was the main attraction in Munich with the France star scoring a fine hat-trick against the winless Bundesliga strugglers.
Wearing a special kit to celebrate the start of Oktoberfest, it was clear that Bayern were in party mood from the start.
They took the lead in the 18th minute with an explosive opener by Jamal Musiala. Alphonso Davies cut the ball back to Musiala on the edge of the box, and the German let fly with a bullet shot.
Kane's moment arrived in the 39th minute from the penalty spot after Olise was tripped. Kane slammed home the spot-kick for his milestone strike.
- An impressive result -

Bayern quickly turned two into three before half-time through a fine first-time strike by Olise, who stylishly caressed his shot into the top corner from the edge of the box - but the best from Olise was yet to come.
An early second-half flurry forced Manuel Neuer into two saves in quick succession. The first saw him deny a golden chance for Janik Haberer, whose miss was as good as it got for the visitors.
Union went 4-0 down in the 54th minute when Olise was allowed to pick out Kane with a sumptuous cross from the right, inviting Kane to glance in his second of the night.

Bayern coach Vincent Kompany sent on Ismael Saibari just after the hour and within seven minutes he scored his first Bayern goal. Davies found the Morocco star, who shrugged off his marker and thumped in Bayern's fifth.
Olise added his second of the night three minutes later to make it six, rounding Ronnow and sending his shot in off the near post.
The Frenchman secured his hat-trick another three minutes later bending in a stunning shot from outside the box.
"We're a bit sad that there's now a short break coming up, as we might lose our rhythm a little," Bayern's sporting director Max Eberl told reporters.
"We wanted to go into the international break with an impressive result. We managed that.
"The team showed that when we play at that level, it's hard to keep up with us."
This ruthless victory is Bayern's biggest margin of victory since their 8-1 win over Wolfsburg in January and, for now, puts the champions top of the table.

Freiburg and Borussia Dortmund, the only teams with 100 per cent records this season, can return to the Bundesliga summit on Saturday when they take on Eintracht Frankfurt and Stuttgart respectively.-AFP

67d6b68af734eaa7: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news" about his administration.
The 80-year-old Republican – who has long had a fiery relationship with the media – warned that other outlets could face a similar fate but did not say which ones.
The move by Trump drew immediate accusations that it was unconstitutional and would be thrown out by the courts, while the impacted news outlets said they would not be cowed.

"I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW...and Politico...from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Trump said on his Truth Social platform.
Trump did not say what prompted the move but added that "media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States."
Later in the Oval Office, Trump told reporters: "I think that somebody has a right to keep them away if they're going to write false stories all the time."
Asked if any particular stories had sparked the ban, he replied: "It's really just cumulative stories over the last two years."
"You get sick of it," he said. "They purposely write negative news, and they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration."

US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth, a former Fox News host who has brought in tight restrictions at the Pentagon, backed Trump's new ban and accused the outlets of having "endangered troops" with unspecified stories.
- 'ILLEGAL ASSAULT' -
Journalists for broadcasters CNN and MS NOW – which was until recently known as MSNBC – and Politico remained on White House premises following Trump's announcement.
Reporters for the two TV news channels could still be seen broadcasting from their stations on the White House driveway.
CNN said Trump's ban was an "illegal assault" on US press freedom, adding that its reporting was "fair and accurate" and was protected under the US Constitution.
Politico vowed Friday to "vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them."

The White House Correspondents Association – the independent body representing journalists covering the presidency – said it "stands in defence" of the journalists "who are being singled out for doing their jobs."
Both of Trump's White House terms have seen him lash out repeatedly at media whose coverage displeases him.
He has filed multiple defamation suits against news outlets, attacked the press on Truth Social and verbally assaulted several reporters, notably women, including CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins.
- 'FLATLY UNCONSTITUTIONAL' -
But it is rare for US presidents to outright bar news outlets – although Trump banned CNN reporter Jim Acosta in his first term, a ban which a court subsequently overturned.
Last year, Trump barred The Associated Press from some events because of the news agency's decision to continue referring to the "Gulf of Mexico" – and not the "Gulf of America" as decreed by Trump.

It has also put stricter controls on journalists in Trump's second term, including taking control of which outlets can cover events as part of the "pool" admitted to tight spaces such as the Oval Office and Air Force One.
Trump's surprise announcement on Friday comes at a time when his approval ratings are at record lows and his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November's midterm elections.
The war in Iran and rising prices, particularly at the gas pump, are among the factors that have contributed to his sinking political fortunes.
Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said a ban on the media outlets would be "flatly unconstitutional."

"The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," Brown said. "This is textbook viewpoint discrimination and will be quickly struck down by the courts if challenged." --AFP

1c38aee02adb2974: PETALING JAYA: A parents’ group says Malaysia’s 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) results highlight the strong link between students’ socioeconomic backgrounds and their academic performance.

Parent Action Group for Education (PAGE) chairman Noor Azimah Abdul Rahim said the country’s science results showed an 82-point gap between students from the top 25% and bottom 25% of socioeconomic backgrounds – a difference equivalent to nearly three years of schooling.

“This is a social mobility issue. It shows family background still has a big influence on a student's achievement, unfortunately,” she said when appearing as a guest on yesterday’s episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast.
“Schools should be the solution. They should reduce the gap a child brings from home, not a place where the gap becomes clearer.
“That’s why intervention needs to be focused on the students and schools that need support most, not a one-size-fits-all approach.”
Noor Azimah was responding to a question from host Khairy Jamaluddin on the widening gap between urban, more affluent schools and rural schools, where the students are from lower-income families.
The former minister said the 82-point gap in science scores showed “quite a large” difference between urban or affluent-area schools and those in more rural areas, which he said was concerning.
Both Noor Azimah and Khairy said this pointed to a broader theme running through the 2025 Pisa results – that Malaysia’s education challenges may not be solvable through curriculum reform alone.

They pointed instead to classroom-level factors - including teacher workload, administrative burdens and the quality of teacher-student engagement – as more likely drivers of uneven outcomes than the content of the syllabus itself.

Malaysian students’ Pisa performance in science in 2025 rose three points to 419. Reading increased five points to 393, while mathematics fell 11 points to 397, continuing a decline recorded in the 2018 and 2022 assessments.

Administered by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Pisa is a triennial survey of 15-year-old students that assesses their acquisition of key knowledge and skills needed for full participation in society.
Only 35% of Malaysian students met the baseline proficiency level in mathematics, meaning nearly two-thirds could not reliably apply basic mathematical reasoning to real-world problems.
Khairy also highlighted a paradox in last year's Pisa results: while mathematics scores had declined, Malaysian students performed better than expected in computational problem-solving.
“Interestingly, 82.6% of Malaysian students performed better than expected. They were among the highest, in the top six,” Azimah said.
“This suggests our children have the ability to adapt, use resources and solve problems when the learning context differs.
“So the question is, why doesn’t that strength translate into basic maths mastery? Again, maybe we need to look at how we teach, not just what we teach.”
072b66b0163a2906: AMSTERDAM: Netherlands' record scorer Memphis Depay was left out, but captain Virgil van Dijk continues his international career as new coach Xavi Hernandez named his first squad on Friday for the upcoming Nations League matches.

Depay played only as a substitute at the World Cup earlier this year and remained on a national-record 55 goals. His omission was widely expected and could signal the end of the 32-year-old striker's international career after 112 appearances.

Van Dijk said last month that he would consider his international future after speaking to the new coach but has decided to continue. The Netherlands face Germany, Greece and Serbia twice in four Nations League matches during the extended three-week international window.

Xavi handed a first call-up to Ruben van Bommel and Gjivai Zechiel and brought back midfielder Joey Veerman but must do without talisman Frenkie de Jong, who is still suffering from a knee injury sustained at the World Cup.
Marten de Roon and Wout Weghorst are also not included in the 26-man squad, along with Guus Til and injured Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Mats Wieffer.
Jeremie Frimpong, Kenneth Taylor and Jurrien Timber, who missed the World Cup, return to the squad.

56f56c59760cd3e1: QUITO: Ecuadoran firefighters backed by helicopters on Friday battled a major blaze on a hill overlooking the capital Quito that has led to the evacuation of dozens of people.
Four helicopters were deployed to extinguish the fire on Casitagua hill, where enormous plumes of smoke were rising into the air.
On the ground, around 100 firefighters were fighting to contain two hotspots, captain Pablo Andino of the Quito Fire Department told AFP.
The area has "a lot of brush and trees, and the wind gusts are causing the fire to spread very quickly," Andino said, noting that firefighters were "at great risk."
It has not rained for over a month in Quito, creating tinder dry conditions that have abetted the outbreak of several fires, eight of which were still active on Friday.
There have been no reports of injuries or damage to homes so far.
Nearly 50 people were evacuated on Thursday from northern Quito as a precautionary measure.
Quito mayor Pabel Munoz estimated the area consumed by flames on Casitagua at around 100 hectares.
Two military and police training academies are situated at the foot of the hill, along with residential complexes.
To prevent the flames from advancing, residents "dug a trench and threw dirt into it," Marta Gonzalez, a 68-year-old seamstress living in the area, told AFP.
City authorities have recorded nearly 200 wildfires between June and September, destroying about 1,200 hectares of forest in the capital.
In 2024, Quito faced one of the worst forest fires in decades, when a blaze started deliberately injured six people and destroyed homes.

64e4b175bb203b48: LONDON: Trent Alexander-Arnold and Cole Palmer were recalled by England on Friday as Thomas Tuchel named his first squad since leaving the pair out of the World Cup.
Real Madrid right-back Alexander-Arnold was included for the first time since June 2025.
Chelsea forward Palmer, in fine form this season, returned after missing out on a place in the squad that reached the World Cup semi-finals before losing to Argentina.

Meanwhile, Rio Ngumoha, Alex Scott and Jarrad Branthwaite were also included in a 27-man group for the three-week, four-game Nations League camp, which comes just nine weeks after England returned home from the United States.

Liverpool's teenage winger Ngumoha, who impressed on his debut against New Zealand in June, and uncapped Bournemouth midfielder Scott are included having been involved the pre-tournament training group in Florida.
Everton defender Branthwaite, whose only cap came in 2024, received a first call-up under Tuchel, with Lewis Hall, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Dominic Calvert-Lewin also returning to England duty.
But Phil Foden, Morgan Gibbs-White and Adam Wharton were among those overlooked for recalls as Tuchel dropped World Cup squad members Ollie Watkins, Ivan Toney and Noni Madueke.
"It's an opportunity for Trent of course. He had a good start to the season, I would say," Tuchel said.
"He started some matches for Real Madrid. They have good results and it's a chance for him to claim what he feels is yours, his place on the right side, so here we go."

In their first game since securing the bronze medal at the World Cup, England face world champions Spain at Wembley in their Nations League opener on Sept 26 before heading to Prague for a game with the Czech Republic three days later.

England then travel to Croatia – a team they beat in the group stages of the World Cup - for a match on Oct 3 before concluding the international window against the Czech Republic at Wembley on Oct 6.

85510df8434ad9c6: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump refused to say whether he would attempt to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, the iconic facility on Washington's Potomac River.
Speaking from the Oval Office, Trump repeated his belief that the centre should append his name to the building in exchange for his work to raise money to renovate the facility.
He falsely claimed the centre faced long-term financial strains that required dramatic action, although the facility posted profits in seven of the past nine years, according to its tax filings.
"I think the Trump administration should be recognised as having saved the Kennedy Center because nobody else remembers," Trump said.

The Kennedy Center board, which has said the facility requires a US$257 million renovation, earlier this week voted to close the facility for two years for the project. US District Judge Christopher Cooper subsequently ordered the Trump administration to explain whether the closure violates a court order limiting its ability to shut down.
Cooper also ordered the administration to provide 30 days' notice before taking steps to demolish the building.

"President Trump is holding the Kennedy Center hostage," said Norm Eisen and Nathaniel Zelinsky, attorneys representing US Representative Joyce Beatty, an Ohio Democrat and ex-officio member of the centre's board who is leading litigation against the administration over its plans for the facility.
Representatives for the centre did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday.

The board, chaired by Trump and controlled by his appointees, earlier this year attempted to rename the facility the "Trump-Kennedy Center" and went so far as to add the president's name to the building. After Cooper ruled that only Congress could rename the centre, the board installed a tarp over the front facade of the building that has remained there as the legal fight continues.
Trump told reporters on Friday that adding his name to the building would be a show of "bipartisanship," because Trump is a Republican and Kennedy, who was assassinated in 1963, was a Democrat.
He called Cooper "hostile," and described the centre — which features a concert hall, opera house, theater and 12 additional performance and meeting spaces — as a "dump."--REUTERS
c7db3f6fb814267d: HAVANA: Cuba was plunged into its seventh massive blackout of the year on Friday as fuel shortages wear on the US-blockaded island.
Just 5% of residents in the Cuban capital Havana had power on Friday evening.
"A total disconnection of the electrical system has occurred," the energy ministry earlier wrote on X.
The nationwide blackout, the 12th since late 2024, occurred after a failure "in the transmission lines" paired with "unstable weather conditions," state-run utility UNE said.
The island of over nine million people endures constant power cuts due to the poor state of its aging thermoelectric plants.
But the situation has worsened significantly since January, when Washington imposed a de facto energy blockade on the island in a bid to pressure Havana's communist government.
A severe lack of fuel makes it difficult to supply Cuba's power plants and backup generators, which typically run on imported diesel.
"It's one thing after another: no water, no gas for cooking, no electricity," schoolteacher Lidia Fernandez, who was just finishing up her workday, told AFP.
"Honestly, I don't know how we haven't gone crazy," the visibly irritated 36-year-old added.
In recent weeks, blackouts have lasted more than 30 hours in the capital, while in outlying provinces, they have sometimes stretched past 60 hours.
Retiree Francisco Rodriguez, 78, told AFP his home had already gone without power for 28 hours on Friday.
"I thought they might at least turn the electricity back on for a few hours soon, but now...I think we won't have light for several days," he said.
The cuts have also affected the island's water supply and mobile phone network, and general living conditions are extremely tough for residents.
"It's no longer just the electricity. We're having problems with water and gas as well," 60-year-old Lazaro Reyes told AFP.
'Problem is growing'
Havana blames the crisis on an array of US-imposed punitive measures, while Washington attributes the hardship to poor internal management.
An economic crisis has engulfed the Caribbean island, where 66% of the population lives in poverty, according to an independent study released this week.
That is compared to 45% in mid-2025, with rising food costs behind the sharp increase in poverty, the research by the Christian Center for Reflection and Dialogue (CCRD) suggests.
The findings give "an indicative picture that the problem is growing," study coordinator Mayra Espina told AFP.
Another retiree, Zunilda Garcia, took the latest blackout in stride, stepping outside to charge a small lamp with solar energy.
"We have to wait and stay calm," Garcia, 60, said. "We can't lose hope."
f04eec9701770a4d: KUALA LUMPUR: Two former prime ministers heaved a sigh of relief this week when one was allowed to serve his jail sentence under home arrest while the other walked free from four money-laundering charges.

The week was capped by a major legal development involving Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest.

This came about after the Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.

Earlier, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was acquitted of four Jana Wibawa-related charges involving RM200 million. Muhyiddin, however, still faces three separate charges in relation to the Jana Wibawa programme.

Also in the dock this week was former minister in the Prime Minister's Department Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom who was charged with transactions involving RM860.3 million in Lembaga Tabung Haji assets.
Below are some of the other major court cases this week.
Najib granted conditional pardon, to serve sentence under house arrest
The decision on Najib's case, however, drew mixed reactions and sparked renewed debate over the use of house arrest for convicted prisoners.
Several quarters also sought clarification on how the arrangement would be implemented and monitored, as the specific conditions attached to Najib's house arrest were not immediately disclosed.

Under the conditional pardon, Najib must comply with the conditions imposed on him, failing which the pardon will be revoked and he will be required to return to prison to serve the remainder of his sentence.
The announcement also drew intense media attention, with reporters gathering outside Kajang Prison and Najib's residence in Langgak Duta, shortly after the decision was made public.
Muhyiddin acquitted of four Jana Wibawa charges
Muhyiddin secured a major legal victory on Tuesday when the High Court acquitted him of four of seven charges linked to the Jana Wibawa programme.
The prosecution informed the court that it did not intend to proceed with one abuse of power charge and three money laundering charges involving RM200 million.
The High Court subsequently granted the Bersatu president a discharge amounting to an acquittal on the four charges.
Muhyiddin, however, still faces three abuse of power charges involving RM25.3 million allegedly received by Bersatu in connection with Jana Wibawa.
The prosecution subsequently closed its case after calling 29 witnesses.
Jamil Khir charged over RM860.3 million in Tabung Haji assets
Jamil Khir was charged at the Sessions Court on Monday with three counts involving RM860.3 million in Tabung Haji assets.
He pleaded not guilty to charges of dishonestly causing the pilgrimage fund to dispose of the assets.
The charges concern transactions involving funds channelled to Al-Rawda Investment for Real Estate Development and Projects Management Co Ltd.
The court fixed bail at RM300,000 in one surety and ordered Jamil Khir to surrender his passport pending disposal of the case.
The case has been fixed for mention on Nov 5.
Teen acquitted in Bandar Utama schoolmate's murder

The Shah Alam High Court acquitted a 15-year-old boy of murdering his 16-year-old schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama after finding that he was of unsound mind at the time of the killing.
The teenager had been charged with stabbing the victim multiple times at the school last year.
The court found that he was suffering from severe schizophrenia and ordered him to be detained at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for a period to be approved by the Sultan of Selangor.

The decision sparked renewed public attention after the victim's mother, Wong Lee Ping, urged the public to support a petition calling on the Attorney-General's Chambers to appeal against the acquittal.
She said the family respected the court and legal process but hoped the case would receive further consideration through any appeal available under the law.
Rosmah's fresh evidence bid put on hold
Rosmah's attempt to introduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid corruption case was put on hold this week.
The Court of Appeal allowed the prosecution's application to stay an earlier order permitting Rosmah to adduce the evidence pending an appeal to the Federal Court.
The evidence involves prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, a former consultant for Jepak Holdings Sdn Bhd.
The stay means further evidence from Rayyan will not be recorded for the time being.
Girl mauled by dog awarded more than RM500,000
A Johor court awarded more than RM500,000 in damages to a 10-year-old girl who suffered serious injuries after she was mauled by a dog.
The girl suffered facial fractures, paralysis and permanent scarring following the attack.
The case stood out among this week's proceedings for the severity of the child's injuries and the amount of the damages awarded.
Judicial Commissioner Noradura Hamzah found the dog's owner, fisherman Lim Seer Hao, fully liable for the attack and dismissed his counterclaim against the girl and her parents.
The award comprised RM193,000 in general damages, RM300,000 for future medical expenses and RM24,643.81 in special damages. The court also awarded costs of RM120,000.

139cc9a7e025e8f1: PETALING JAYA: Although Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has been described as a “prime minister‑in‑waiting”, a political analyst argues that other party leaders are equally capable of leading the country — with far less baggage.

Akademi Nusantara’s Azmi Hassan said Umno need not “eliminate” Zahid as party president, though it would augur well for the Barisan Nasional lynchpin to give greater prominence to other senior leaders.
He said Umno deputy president Mohamad Hasan, also known as Tok Mat, as well as vice-presidents Johari Ghani and Khaled Nordin were quite capable of replacing Zahid at the helm of the party.
“Umno needs to give alternatives. It has a very capable lineup of leaders who can replace Zahid when the time comes, such as Tok Mat and Johari.
“These are two very capable leaders without any baggage or liability (unlike Zahid),” he told FMT.
This would be a strategic move, said Azmi, enabling Umno to project a cleaner, anti‑corruption image, given that several party leaders have been tainted by corruption cases.

Zahid himself remains under a cloud. Facing 47 charges in the Yayasan Akalbudi case, the Umno president is seeking a full acquittal, having been granted a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in September 2023.

“So in this particular case, a new breed of leaders, including Khaled, is needed to give the perception that Umno isn't going back to its old ways of just allowing corruption among its leaders,” Azmi said.
“I think that’s very important if Umno and PAS want to form the federal government with the help of Borneo parties like Gabungan Parti Sarawak and Gabungan Rakyat Sabah.”
Last week, former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin labelled Zahid a potential “prime minister‑in‑waiting” following the Umno president’s keynote address at the party’s general assembly.
Khairy, a former Cabinet minister, also described BN as a “government‑in‑waiting”, hinting at the prospect of an Umno‑led federal administration following the next general election (GE16).

Although BN currently holds only 30 parliamentary seats, the Umno‑led coalition’s confidence has been boosted following decisive victories in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, the latter secured through a pact with Perikatan Nasional.
Umno is hoping to build on this momentum in the Melaka state polls, expected to be held by the end of the year, and GE16, which the party wants called sooner rather than later.
However, Oh Ei Sun of the Singapore Institute of International Affairs dismissed the notions of prime minister- and government‑in‑waiting as nothing more than an “election bluff”.
“It’s just an attempt to create momentum and so on, it’s nothing more than that,” he said.
8cc57f2cd1a48e6e: PETALING JAYA: Walaupun Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi disebut sebagai ‘bakal perdana menteri’, seorang penganalisis politik berpandangan parti itu mempunyai beberapa pemimpin lain yang juga mampu menerajui negara dan tidak dibebani kontroversi sama.

Azmi Hassan dari Akademi Nusantara berkata Umno tidak perlu mengetepikan Zahid sebagai presiden, namun parti teras Barisan Nasional (BN) itu wajar memberi lebih banyak ruang kepada beberapa pemimpin kanannya.

Menurutnya, Timbalan Presiden Umno Mohamad Hasan atau Tok Mat, serta Naib Presiden Johari Ghani dan Khaled Nordin antara pemimpin yang berkemampuan mengambil alih kepimpinan parti apabila tiba masanya.
“Umno perlu menawarkan pilihan. Parti itu mempunyai barisan pemimpin yang sangat berkebolehan untuk menggantikan Zahid apabila tiba masanya, seperti Tok Mat dan Johari.
“Kedua-duanya pemimpin yang sangat berkebolehan dan dilihat tidak mempunyai beban atau liabiliti seperti Zahid,” katanya kepada FMT.

Azmi berkata langkah memberi lebih banyak ruang kepada pemimpin berkenaan juga boleh menjadi strategi untuk membantu Umno menampilkan imej yang lebih bersih dan tegas dalam isu rasuah, selepas beberapa pemimpinnya sebelum ini dikaitkan dengan kes rasuah.
Zahid sendiri masih belum memperoleh pembebasan penuh dalam kes Yayasan Akalbudi.
Beliau dilepaskan tanpa dibebaskan DNAA pada September 2023 bagi 47 pertuduhan rasuah, pengubahan wang haram dan pecah amanah, dan kemudian memohon pembebasan penuh.

“Dalam keadaan ini, Umno memerlukan barisan pemimpin baharu, termasuk Khaled, bagi menunjukkan parti itu tidak kembali kepada cara lama dengan membiarkan isu rasuah membayangi kepimpinannya,” kata Azmi.
“Saya fikir perkara ini sangat penting sekiranya Umno dan PAS mahu membentuk kerajaan Persekutuan dengan sokongan parti Borneo seperti Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) dan Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS).”

Minggu lalu, bekas ketua Pemuda Umno Khairy Jamaluddin menyifatkan Zahid sebagai seorang yang berpotensi menjadi ‘prime minister-in-waiting’ susulan ucapan dasar presiden Umno itu pada perhimpunan agung parti.

Khairy, yang juga bekas menteri, turut menyifatkan ucapan itu sebagai datang daripada sebuah ‘government-in-waiting’, sekali gus memberi gambaran mengenai kemungkinan kerajaan Persekutuan diterajui Umno selepas PRU16.
Walaupun BN ketika ini hanya mempunyai 30 kerusi Parlimen, keyakinan gabungan diterajui Umno itu meningkat susulan kemenangan besar dalam PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan.
Di Negeri Sembilan, kerjasama BN-Perikatan Nasional (PN) berjaya memperoleh majoriti dua pertiga apabila kedua-duanya memenangi 25 daripada 36 kerusi DUN.
Umno kini berharap dapat meneruskan momentum itu pada PRN Melaka yang dijangka berlangsung sebelum akhir tahun, selain PRU16 yang mahu diadakan lebih awal.

Bagaimanapun, Oh Ei Sun dari Singapore Institute of International Affairs melihat gambaran mengenai ‘bakal perdana menteri’ dan ‘kerajaan menunggu’ itu sebagai tidak lebih daripada gertakan menjelang pilihan raya.
“Ia sekadar usaha untuk membina momentum dan sebagainya. Tidak lebih daripada itu,” katanya.
425d776bc9c70ba4: PETALING JAYA: At nearly 8,000m above sea level, Mohd Khafiz Bachok suddenly found himself worrying less about his own condition than that of the Sherpa beside him.
They were resting at Camp Four on Mount Everest, deep in the so-called "death zone", when Saila Mingma, 26, told him his body had gone numb.

Khafiz, 47, urged him to put his oxygen mask back on before they both closed their eyes and tried to rest. “During a climb, he cannot climb alone, and I cannot climb alone either, so we really depend on each other," he told Bernama.
That moment of concern has become one of the most telling scenes in “Tekad: Ekspedisi Guthrie Everest 2026”, a documentary about Khafiz's successful ascent of Mount Everest on May 18.
More popularly known as Kicok, he became the 27th Malaysian to reach the summit, while for Saila it marked a sixth successful ascent.
But director Ahmad Yazid, 42, was less interested in simply recording another summit achievement than in showing the relationship that made it possible.
He said one scene, in which Saila helps pull up and zip Kicok’s hood during the climb, says as much as the later moment when Kicok checks on Saila at Camp Four.
“Many documentaries focus on the pride of the climb itself, and we know that reaching the summit is indeed something to be proud of,” Ahmad said.
“But we know less about the relationship between a climber and his Sherpa in making that climb a success.”

Ahmad, who has directed acclaimed documentaries including "Al-Maunah: The Malaysian Arms Heist" (2009) and "The Murder of Canny Ong" (2010), as well as produced content for Discovery Channel and National Geographic, said the two men shared far more than a route up the mountain.
“They smiled together, they laughed together, they got sick together, and success depended on the two-way relationship between the two individuals making the climb.”

That trust extended to the filming itself. Kicok had previously recorded footage while climbing K2 in Pakistan and Mount Manaslu in Nepal, giving the production team enough confidence to place cameras in his hands again on Everest.

Before the climb, Ahmad and director of photography Marwan Murshid briefed Kicok and Saila on the footage they hoped to capture. Once the ascent began, however, the filmmakers had no live video feed and could only communicate by radio.
“I could only put my faith in him. Whether he pressed record or not, I wouldn’t know,” Ahmad added.
The production team prepared action cameras, a 360-degree camera, extra batteries and memory cards - but high-altitude conditions remained unpredictable.
Case in point: at around 5,400m near Crampon Point, Ahmad said temperatures suddenly dropped to about -30°C while the crew was filming. They could only soldier on.
The 50-minute documentary also follows Chew Wei Ngor, better known as Margaret, 56, who reached Camp Four but had to abandon her attempt to summit because of congestion along the route.
For Kicok, the documentary captures something that summit photographs alone cannot show: the constant need to watch over the person climbing beside you.
Produced by Rack Focus Films and Red Communications and supported by the Finas Content Fund, "Tekad" was aired recently in conjunction with National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.
f75d95aac7edf76a: KOTA BHARU: A man weighing 250kg who died of an obesity-related condition has been buried with the help of the Malaysian civil defence force at the Gual Tinggi Islamic cemetery in Rantau Panjang.
Civil defence officer Fuad Ismail said the health ministry contacted the civil defence yesterday morning to assist in moving the body for the burial.
“The operation lasted nearly five hours, starting from 11am, involving several of our personnel, and a lorry to transport the body.
"The local villagers also lent a hand to facilitate the burial arrangements,” he said in a statement last night.

The man, aged 23, was from Kampung Gual Tinggi, Rantau Panjang. His body was taken from Universiti Sains Malaysia Hospital in Kubang Kerian to Masjid Al-Hidayah for the funeral prayer before he was buried.
b066b060ea703195: WASHINGTON: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will brief the UN Security Council next week during the annual gathering of world leaders for the UN General Assembly, the company said Friday.

The meeting is being organized by France, which currently holds the rotating presidency of the 15-member Security Council, and comes as major players in the industry have said a slowdown in AI development could be necessary out of safety concerns.
UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres on Wednesday called for coordinated international action to address AI risks as fears rise about the dangers of the fast-evolving technology.
"National action is essential. But global coordination is also indispensable," Guterres told reporters.
Concerns about AI safety have escalated in recent weeks, with workers at major AI developers resigning over concerns about the dangers posed by the technology.
Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei published an essay soon after urging caution.
"We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.
Altman and tech titan Elon Musk lent their support to the idea, as did Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis, who himself has called for a US-led global regulatory body for the technology.
President Donald Trump has dismissed warnings against AI risks as a "hoax" and pushed back against calls for tighter oversight.
37803553b08be186: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them of reporting "fiction and lies" about his administration.
Trump added that "other Fake News Media Outlets" would face a similar fate, but did not say which ones.
The move by Trump, who has long had a fiery relationship with the media, drew immediate accusations that it was unconstitutional and would be thrown out by the courts.

"I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW...and Politico...from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Trump said on his Truth Social platform.

The 80-year-old Republican did not say what had prompted the move but added that "media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America."
Later in the Oval Office, Trump told reporters: "I think that somebody has a right to keep them away if they're going to write false stories all the time."
Asked if any particular stories had sparked the ban, he replied: "It's really just cumulative stories over the last two years."
"You get sick of it," he said. "They're smart people, but they purposely write negative news, and they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration."

For the time being, journalists for news outlet Politico, and broadcasters CNN and MS Now -- which was until recently known as MSNBC -- were still on White House premises following Trump's announcement.
CNN and MS Now reporters could still be seen broadcasting from their stations on the driveway of the White House.
CNN said Trump's plan to ban the outlets from the White House was an "illegal assault" on US press freedom.

The network said its reporting was "fair and accurate" and was protected under the US Constitution, adding that a ban "would be an illegal assault on that fundamental and constitutionally-protected right."
'Flatly unconstitutional'
Politico vowed Friday to "vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them."
The news outlet also said Trump's claims that it had received government subsidies were false and had been "thoroughly debunked."
Trump and the White House have long been critical of CNN and MS NOW, with the US president frequently sparring with CNN reporters in particular during encounters in the Oval Office.

It is extremely rare for US presidents to outright bar news outlets from the White House, although Trump banned CNN reporter Jim Acosta in his first term and Richard Nixon put restrictions on The Washington Post over its reporting on the Watergate scandal.

But in his second term, Trump's administration has put stricter controls on journalists, including taking control of which members of the press can cover events as part of the "pool" admitted to tight spaces such as the Oval Office and Air Force One.
Last year, Trump barred The Associated Press from some events because of the news agency's decision to continue referring to the "Gulf of Mexico" -- and not the "Gulf of America" as decreed by Trump.
Both of Trump's White House terms have seen him lash out repeatedly at media whose coverage displeases him.
Trump has filed multiple defamation suits against news outlets, attacked the press on Truth Social and verbally assaulted several reporters, notably women.
Trump's surprise announcement on Friday comes at a time when his approval ratings are at record lows and his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November's midterm elections.
The war in Iran and rising prices, particularly at the gas pump, are among the factors that have contributed to his sinking political fortunes.
Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said a ban on the media outlets would be "flatly unconstitutional".

"The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," Brown said. "This is textbook viewpoint discrimination and will be quickly struck down by the courts if challenged."

72e802559596442b: LISBON: Cristiano Ronaldo has been included in new Portugal manager Jorge Jesus' first 25-man squad for the defending champions' upcoming four Nations League matches.
In August, Ronaldo fuelled speculation about his retirement plans after saying the coming year would probably be the last of his playing career.

The 41-year-old Portugal captain is one of the most decorated players in soccer history, having won major trophies with Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and current club Al-Nassr since making his senior debut for Sporting in 2002.

Ronaldo, a five-time Ballon d'Or winner, was unable to add a World Cup title to his list of honours after Portugal were knocked out in the last 16 by eventual champions Spain, leaving the sport's biggest prize absent from his trophy cabinet.

"Cris is a player like any other. If he performs, he plays; if not, he doesn't. He has a different status - he has five Ballon d'Or awards - but does that factor into my decisions? No. However, the fact that he is different is."

Jesus will make his debut as Portugal manager against Wales at home on September 24. Portugal then travel to face Norway and Denmark on September 27 and October 1 respectively, before hosting Norway on October 4.

e99b75d05995840d: FRANKFURT: German auto giant Volkswagen warned Friday of a 10-billion-euro hit to its annual earnings, citing tough conditions in China, problems at subsidiary Porsche and restructuring costs.

Europe's biggest carmaker, in the process of pushing through the global auto industry's largest job-cutting drive, said it expected a profit margin of just 1% for 2026, down from a previous forecast of between four and 5.5%.
Like its peers, Volkswagen has struggled with the costs of transitioning to electric vehicles as well as falling demand and cut-throat competition in China, the world's largest car market.
The Volkswagen and Audi marques were particularly feeling the heat in China, the 10-brand group said Friday.
"The situation on global markets has continued to worsen -- particularly in China", VW finance boss Arno Antlitz said in an interview on the company intranet.

"Demand for battery-electric vehicles has accelerated, partly against the backdrop of the geopolitical situation and a sharp rise in petrol prices, and we currently earn significantly less from these than from internal combustion engine cars," he added.
Volkswagen also said it had written down the value of Porsche by €6 billion, citing more modest expectations of the sports-car maker's future performance.
Porsche sales have cratered in China and it has struggled to shift its electric models, which lack the noisy thrill of petrol engines, leading to costly strategy changes.

The Porsche write-down is Volkswagen's second in a year. It booked a 5.1-billion-euro hit last September after the luxury carmaker rejigged its product portfolio, shifting away from EVs, and cut profit targets.

On Friday VW booked another two billion euros in charges, linked to write-downs of VW assets in China, the sale of a plant in northern Germany and the expansion of early retirement schemes, the company said.

VW said earlier this month it would offload its Osnabrueck plant, in northwest Germany to Israeli investors and the German state of Lower Saxony, a major VW shareholder, with an initial air-defence project planned for the Israeli firm Rafael Advanced Defence Systems.
The carmaker also narrowed its sales outlook for the year, saying it expected a slight fall to about €315 billion. It had previously forecast sales to be flat or fall by up to three percent.
VW shares plunged 7.55% after the announcement. Fellow German carmakers Mercedes-Benz and BMW both fell over 5%.
Volkswagen earlier this month struck a deal with unions to axe up to 100,000 jobs by 2030, increasing by 50,000 the number of expected cuts across the group.
Unions have organised nationwide protests Monday outside car manufacturers and their suppliers, demanding more action to help the ailing industry.
67f56fd11612f8de: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest arrangement could revive his political influence and inject fresh energy into sections of Umno's grassroots, analysts said.

The move could reignite the "Bossku" sentiment and strengthen Najib's role as a symbol and rallying point for traditional supporters, they said, while easing some pressure within Umno over his imprisonment.
But they cautioned that the political impact would not be uniform and could create fresh challenges for the unity government.

Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said the decision could have an immediate psychological effect on Umno members who regard Najib's imprisonment as a longstanding political grievance.
He said Najib retained sentimental value among sections of Umno's grassroots despite having spent years in prison and his return home could improve morale among his supporters.

"The decision gives relief to Najib's supporters and sections of the Umno grassroots. It could revive the 'Bossku' sentiment and strengthen the feeling among supporters that the party leadership had fought for Najib," he told the New Straits Times.
He said this could allow Umno to move beyond the prolonged focus on Najib's imprisonment and concentrate on strengthening its organisation and preparing for the next general election.
But he cautioned that any boost in morale among Najib's supporters should not be interpreted as an automatic increase in wider public support for Umno.
He said Najib's association with the 1Malaysia Development Bhd scandal and questions surrounding governance and integrity would continue to influence how some voters viewed the development.

National Unity Advisory Council member and political analyst Professor Datuk Dr Awang Azman Awang Pawi said the decision could provide "moral and psychological relief" to Najib's core supporters and sections of the Umno grassroots.

He said Najib could regain greater influence as a political symbol and driver of grassroots sentiment, even while remaining subject to the requirements of the conditional pardon and unable to necessarily return to political activity as before.
"Najib has the potential to become more influential as a symbol and driver of grassroots sentiment.

"He could become an asset to Umno in strengthening the loyalty of traditional supporters, particularly Malay voters who view him as a leader who brought stability and provided assistance to the people."
He said the development could also increase pressure within Umno for the party to be more vocal in defending Najib and raising issues surrounding justice and his pardon.
But Umno must handle the issue carefully as it is still part of the unity government, he added.
"The party cannot be seen as turning the decision into a political victory that challenges the sensitivities of its partners in Pakatan Harapan."

Universiti Malaya Department of Political Science, Public Administration and Development Studies senior lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the decision could ease tensions among Najib's strongest supporters while creating political risks for the unity government.
"This decision provides moral and psychological relief to Najib's staunch supporters and part of the Umno grassroots.
"In the immediate term, it could revive the 'Bossku' sentiment and increase internal pressure for Umno to be more vocal in raising issues of justice, pardon and defending its former president."
He said Umno must balance the renewed sentiment around Najib with its position in the unity government.
He said Najib could regain influence as a political symbol and mobiliser among traditional Umno supporters, particularly Malay voters who continue to associate him with stability and aid.

"Najib can become influential again as a symbol and driver of grassroots sentiment. Although he remains subject to the conditions of the pardon and is not necessarily free to engage in politics as usual, he can become an asset to Umno in strengthening the loyalty of traditional supporters."
